problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{arccos}⁡y}{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.$*

activity_context.topic_title: Changing the Order of Integration in Triple Integrals: Changing Projection

feedback.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.$*
feedback.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le e,\,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡z\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{3}y}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/14c67512e143995cbfcfcf9e80c8d0975bbbc42368c97aa29956bd2d3f3454a8.png)

The region $D$ is type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le e,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡z\le y\le 1}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
z=1
$$

and the top boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $z=z(y),$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡z\,⟹\,z={e}^{y}.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,1\le z\le {e}^{y}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/d18470b45d21b4734187c1f639784a4e75924ed212e3fa4c7a214d19eaeb6022.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}y}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}{[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{y})]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{3}y}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}\operatorname{arctan}⁡\sqrt{3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}\frac{\pi }{3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[\frac{\pi }{3}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{y}}\text{d}z]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{\pi }{3}[z]_{1}^{{e}^{y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{\pi }{3}({e}^{y}-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}[{e}^{y}-y]_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}(e-1-1+0) \\  & =\frac{\pi (e-2)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
